html:
The railways of French Senegal and Sudan: the line from Dakar to Saint-Louis, opened in 1885, the first in West Africa, and the line from Dakar to Bamako on the Niger, completed in 1923.

They opened the interior to the groundnut trade and made Dakar the port of French Sudan, now Mali. Building them cost many workers' lives and the independence of Cayor. African railway workers struck for equal pay from October 1947 to March 1948, a famous event of the independence era that Ousmane Sembene made into his novel God's Bits of Wood. The line decayed after 2000 and was largely out of use by the 2010s.
